trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court No.1, Kamrup, Guwahati, Assam in Misc (J) Case No. 157/2018
case_name: Sri Manash Sarma v. Smt. Maitreyee Sabhapandit — Mat.App./15/2022
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2015 and lived together initially. The husband's work required him to travel frequently, leading to the wife staying alone in their flat. She claimed maintenance pendente lite and cost of proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's maintenance claim is not necessarily defeated by the other spouse's financial difficulties.
legal_principles.held: It was contended that the husband used to pay Rs.8,000/- (Rupees eight thousand) only to Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) only since marriage although she was employed as a Teacher in School until the month of October, 2016.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's maintenance claim can be based on the other spouse's ability to pay, not just their actual income.
legal_principles.held: He denied the contentions of the respondent wife that she is an unemployed person. He also denied the contentions of the respondent wife regarding the payment of expenditure incurred in respect of the flat in which the respondent wife had been residing since her marriage with the husband.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed. The order dated 22.02.2019 passed by Principal Judge, Family Court No.1, Kamrup, Guwahati, Assam in Misc (J) Case No. 157/2018 is set aside.
